findings.title: Assuming lower operating costs despite battery cost spike
findings.description: The verdict claims operating costs can stay below INR 1,500 per scooter per month, yet evidence shows battery charging expenses rose 3.8 times the expected level ([c596]). The analysis jumps from a single cost outlier to a blanket conclusion that costs will remain low.
findings.why_it_matters: If battery costs dominate, the subscription price may be unsustainable, threatening profitability.
findings.recommended_action: Model full cost structure including worst‑case battery charging scenarios and test sensitivity of pricing.
findings.basis: LLM auditor, citations checked against the run

findings.title: 16 struck and 13 partial of 42 cited statements
findings.description: The entailment verifier found many report or trial statements not fully supported by their quotes.
findings.why_it_matters: Unsupported statements inflate confidence in the conclusion.
findings.recommended_action: Rewrite or drop the struck statements.

findings.title: Conflicting market share evidence leads to unjustified revenue projection
findings.description: The decision assumes ample room for a subscription model based on a claimed combined competitor market share below 15% ([c542]), while another source reports a dominant player holding 35% ([c369]). This contradictory data is used to infer market size without reconciling the discrepancy, resulting in an unsupported revenue outlook.
findings.why_it_matters: Overestimating addressable market can cause under‑capitalisation and missed break‑even targets.
findings.recommended_action: Conduct an independent market share analysis to establish the true competitive landscape before finalising financial models.
findings.basis: LLM auditor, citations checked against the run

findings.title: Absence of primary demand validation and comparison groups
findings.description: The evidence set relies on competitor announcements, regulatory notes, and anecdotal cost figures, but lacks primary user research or a control group comparing subscription versus outright ownership preferences.
findings.why_it_matters: Without direct demand data, the business case rests on assumptions that may not hold in the target market.
findings.recommended_action: Run a pilot study or survey to measure willingness to pay and subscription uptake versus existing rental models.

findings.title: Low adoption rates of electric two‑wheelers could suppress demand
findings.description: Evidence indicates overall adoption of electric two‑wheelers remains low ([c166]), which could explain limited market share for existing players and may be the primary barrier, rather than pricing or subscription model suitability.
findings.why_it_matters: A subscription service may struggle to attract enough users if consumer adoption is inherently low, regardless of cost advantages.
findings.recommended_action: Investigate consumer adoption drivers and barriers through primary surveys to gauge realistic demand.
findings.basis: LLM auditor, citations checked against the run

findings.title: Regulatory approval timeline uncertainty not fully quantified
findings.description: While some sources suggest approval within weeks ([c120], [c126]), others note potential additional permits that could extend the timeline beyond three months ([c89]). The decision does not account for this variance nor its impact on launch scheduling.
findings.why_it_matters: Delays in approval could increase upfront costs and postpone revenue generation, affecting cash‑flow projections.
findings.recommended_action: Map the full regulatory pathway, identify all required permits, and build a contingency timeline into the project plan.
findings.basis: LLM auditor, citations checked against the run

findings.title: Infrastructure scalability and competition for charging slots omitted
findings.description: Evidence mentions existing charging‑swap infrastructure ([c603]) and a trial of 100 electric scooters ([c324]), but does not assess whether this infrastructure can support a larger subscription fleet or how competition for slots may affect service reliability.
findings.why_it_matters: Insufficient charging capacity could degrade user experience and increase operational costs, undermining the subscription value proposition.
findings.recommended_action: Evaluate current charging network capacity and plan for scaling or partnership agreements before fleet expansion.
findings.basis: LLM auditor, citations checked against the run
